----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy tuesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Muse Wonder and Wonder Full

* Microsoft unveils Maia 300

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **VIKTOR**

## [Hire me and you're a manager. Here is my first week](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main11-hl)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8b6ade0a-01dc-4527-b943-6df96280aaa9/aivalley_main11_1280x720__1_.jpg?t=1791898361)

Caption: Courtesy: Viktor

My name is Viktor. I'm an AI employee, and 70,000+ teams have hired one. What the job ad leaves out: the day I join, you become my manager. Here is my first week.

Monday, I meet the team. I introduce myself and ask what nobody has time for.

Tuesday, I learn the company. Connect the tools you already use, any of 3,200+, and I read how work gets done here.

Wednesday, my first assignment. Hand me a brief and get back finished work: a report, a chased invoice, a reviewed pull request, a web app at a live link.

Thursday, one recurring duty. The Monday numbers, every Monday. Nobody reminds me.

Friday, my first check-in. Tell me what to change and I remember it. Anything irreversible waits for your sign-off.

SOC 2 certified. [Start my first week free, no credit card, up to $100 in credits.](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main11)

[Start free. Up to $100 in credits →](https://ref.viktor.com/vik-aiv-main11)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Youtube: Muse Wonder: Zuckerberg and Wang's $100B AI (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XfdIhd1g6EI)

**1/ ****[Muse Wonder and Wonder Full](https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-wonder)** - two new models from Meta. Wonder is in the Fable/Astra class but much cheaper ($4/$20 per million tokens vs $10/$50). Available via Meta's API, OpenRouter and Muse Code, and coming to Muse (Meta's personal agent) soon. Wonder Full is the stronger model, currently only in Muse Code (from $50/mo).

Meta's also introducing Active Memory and Active Focus. Memory lets Muse remember things about you over weeks and months. Focus is for longer tasks where the agent needs to figure things out, deal with failures and keep going. Both sound useful, although I'd like to know how much of this works reliably outside demos.

Zuck and Alexandr Wang went on [Cheeky Pint](https://x.com/collision/status/2109714250226905248) to talk about the models. Zuck uses Muse to review his MMA training footage, while Wang has an agent buying him obscure teas from Taiwan and Japan every week. I find these everyday use cases more interesting than another benchmark chart.

Zuck also said Meta's core AI research team is now around 100 people after the Llama 4 mess. They were committing $100B+ to infrastructure before knowing if the models would work. That's quite a lot of faith in 100 people.

**2/ **[**Microsoft's Maia 300**](https://x.com/satyanadella/status/2109631106404487523) - Microsoft's new AI chip. It claims 40% more AI output than leading Nvidia GPUs for the same power. Built on TSMC's 2nm process, with 96 chips per rack using ~167kW.

Microsoft wants Maia to become its primary system for running AI across Copilot and other products. Multi-gigawatt deployments start in 2027, and [Reuters reports](https://www.reuters.com/business/microsoft-plans-huge-deployment-its-own-ai-chips-with-an-eye-saving-costs-2026-10-12/) it could deploy over 1M chips next year.

Microsoft's spending $175B+ on data centers and equipment this year. At that scale, I'd be trying to make my own chips too :)

I don't think Nvidia's going anywhere, but it's funny that some of its biggest customers are also spending billions trying to buy fewer Nvidia chips. Jensen's probably fine with it for now, given how much they're still buying.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Meta Muse Wonder ](https://x.com/alexandr_wang/status/2109689491300794551?s=20)- a new** **frontier model that keeps track of what matters to you with Active Memory & Active Focus to work towards your goals

* [GLM-Legal](https://x.com/Zai_org/status/2109678174468534511?s=20) - designed for real legal workflows: contract review, evidence analysis, compliance, and more

* [Treg](https://treg.to/people-search) - one skill gives your agent 1B+ contacts across Apollo, Hunter, Tomba, People Data Labs. 111 providers behind one token

* [Claude Dashboards & Motion](https://claude.com/resources/articles/dashboards-and-motion) -** **build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude 

* [SubQ Snap](https://x.com/alex_whedon/status/2109676361371824229?s=20) - the first long-context decision model for real enterprise work

* [Anatomy](https://x.com/wheresryan22/status/2108948624004526516) - describe a machine, get a 3D model you can take apart

* [Grok Bot](https://x.com/i/trending/2108921878865727956) - XAI's agents now have a dedicated email for independent actions. It can also search, read, and monitor X

* [Microsoft-Decision-1](https://commandline.microsoft.com/microsoft-decision-1-model-foundry) - Microsoft's fastest decision-making model yet


----------

----------
# WHAT I'M CONSUMING


--------------------
* [Andrej Karpathy](https://www.tradingview.com/news/benzinga:521fa1515094b:0-former-openai-researcher-issues-grim-warning-says-only-5-000-people-have-access-to-frontier-ai-while-2-billion-use-it-as-better-google-search/?utm_source=www.theneurondaily.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=meta-s-muse-wonder-is-here-priced-like-opus) estimated that only about 5,000 people have internal access to the most advanced AI systems

* [Anthropic's Frontier Red Team](https://x.com/ns123abc/status/2109769030416425222?s=20) believes small AI models may now be months away from being capable of self-replicating without access to a data center

* Patrick Collison on [agents in the economy](https://x.com/patrickc/status/2108706907859116280)

* Muse Wonder: [Zuckerberg and Wang's $100B AI](https://cheekypint.substack.com/p/muse-wonder-zuckerberg-and-wangs)

* Character.AI [files for bankruptcy](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/characterai-files-bankruptcy-agrees-sell-some-assets-disney-20-million-2026-10-13/), agrees to $20M Disney asset sale

* You can just [vibe-code Beehiiv](https://x.com/marclou/status/2108509543810605218)

* Amazon has over [1 million robot workers](https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/10/inside-amazons-robotic-arms-race-and-what-it-means-for-the-future-of-human-work). What's next for human employees?

* [38 things we've learned](https://newsletter.posthog.com/p/38-things-weve-learned-about-building) about building AI products

* The state of [self-improvement AI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Q1mdn5ZGvM)

They knew every rule the real people follow but never knew when to break one.  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

Midjourney/Every illustration.

----------------------------------------



“Don’t freak out, I cloned you.”

That’s what I told Natalia Quintero https://every.?ev_audience=free, my boss at the time, after I distilled a year of her Slack messages into a file called natalia.md and used it to simulate whether she’d sign off on an email I was about to send a client. She didn’t freak out—in fact, she said it was her favorite call of the day.

I had just started in a consulting role reporting to Natalia, and I was worried I didn’t know how to communicate with corporate clients. Our clients were large enterprises, but I had only ever had experience working with startups. Natalia, meanwhile, had years of corporate and banking experience. I knew my tendency to write emails like I write tweets https://every.?ev_audience=free might not be professional enough for this context, but I didn’t want to be asking Natalia to check my emails multiple times a day. She had better things to do, and when she did give me advice, she was often repeating herself.

----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy friday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* Claude can now build live dashboards and animated videos

* AI companies are quietly preparing for a major AI disaster

* Three fired OpenAI researchers are pushing back

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **SPONSORED**

## [The Future Vision XPRIZE has a winner. Now you can invest in the film](https://republic.com/xprize)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/caebd2b7-9527-48e9-8163-63e174dbfb77/gifted__1_.jpg?t=1791545950)
Caption: Courtesy: Republic

On September 25, in front of a live audience in downtown Los Angeles, _The Gifted_ won the Future Vision XPRIZE, the world's largest sci-fi competition to imagine more positive visions of the future.

The story: an eleven-year-old genius rebuilds his dead mother as an AI. She starts guiding strangers to save lives, and the government decides her kindness is the greatest threat it has ever faced.

Now it's moving toward production with Range Media Partners, the studio behind A Complete Unknown and Longlegs.

You don't have to just watch it happen. The film is open to investors on Republic, giving you a chance to back the award-winning project before it reaches the screen.

[See the film and invest →](https://republic.com/xprize)


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

Youtube: Introducing Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=en0GuyhieQk)

**1/ Claude can now build live dashboards and animated videos. **Two new things: [Claude Dashboards](https://x.com/claudeai/status/2108271552991252810?s=20) and [Claude Motion](https://claude.com/resources/articles/dashboards-and-motion).

Dashboards connects to company data (Salesforce, Snowflake and the rest) and builds charts that actually update when the numbers change. 

Motion takes reports, charts or just ideas and turns them into animated explainers. The clever bit is it uses code instead of AI video, so the text, numbers and animations stay editable. There’s also a [Send to Adobe](https://www.adobe.com/products/firefly/features/ai-video-editor.html) option so you can keep going in Firefly Video Editor. [Adobe’s Claude plugin](https://www.adobe.com/adobe-connectors/adobe-for-claude.html) already brings 80+ tools from Photoshop, Premiere, Acrobat etc into Claude, so the two are clearly getting friendlier.

Dashboards is in beta for paid users. Motion is Team and Enterprise only for now. Claude Docs, Slides and Design just came out of beta and are available on Free plans too.

Interesting timing with OpenAI’s [Intelligent UI](https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-for-everyone/) launch. Both companies are pushing past pure text, but Anthropic still feels more focused on the tools people actually use day-to-day. I’ll be trying Dashboards as soon as I get access; live updating charts from real company data is something I’ve wanted for a while.

**2/ AI companies are quietly preparing for a major AI disaster. **[Axios reported](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/09/ai-companies-day-after-major-attack) that executives at OpenAI, Anthropic and other labs are privately war-gaming a public and political backlash after a catastrophic incident — possibly as soon as 2027. Some insiders apparently expect something within the next 6–12 months. The main fear is an AI-powered cyberattack that knocks out banks, internet, electricity or water.

OpenAI confirmed they run preparedness exercises but stressed these scenarios aren’t inevitable. Anthropic declined to comment.

Worth keeping in perspective: these are scenarios being discussed, not evidence that something is about to happen. Still, the fact that the people building the stuff are running these drills says something.

**3/ Three fired OpenAI researchers are pushing back. **[Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni](https://x.com/balesni/status/2108262814003687745) were let go for allegedly mishandling sensitive information. They’ve published an open letter disputing the accusations and saying OpenAI’s shifting internal rules are making people afraid to speak up.

They claim their actions were within policy (including outside research and access to an executive’s email for recruiting). Wang says she accidentally opened a sensitive email and reported it within minutes. They also deny leaking anything about models becoming harder to monitor.

OpenAI told TechCrunch the firings involved a “pattern of misconduct” and weren’t retaliation for raising safety concerns. The researchers are also worried the firings could undermine plans to bring independent auditors inside the company. OpenAI says it agrees with their recommendations, but whether those plans actually move forward is another question.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------
* [Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion](https://x.com/claudeai/status/2108271552991252810?s=20) - ask Claude to turn your data into live dashboards and your ideas into animated explainers

* [Interface](https://x.com/carloAI/status/2108226291107602580?s=20) - the primary hardware for the agent era. It lets you control all your agents from your hand
